working_title: Rainfall-associated expansion of frog active communities spans spatial and taxonomic dimensions without detectable beta-diversity change
central_claims: Within matched route × seasonal-window comparisons, greater rainfall contrast is associated with a larger acoustically active spatial footprint.
Rainfall contrast is associated with higher local richness among active stops (alpha) and higher route-level active richness (gamma).
Among-active-stop compositional differentiation shows no detectable rainfall-associated change under pairwise Sørensen, turnover, nestedness-resultant, or normalized Whittaker metrics.

Proportional fill of the active species × active-site matrix is practically equivalent across rainfall contrast within a prespecified +/-0.05 connectance-slope margin in both the primary and exact-consecutive-year samples.
The rainfall-associated increase in species × stop incidences is dominated by expansion at spatial and/or taxonomic matrix boundaries rather than rearrangement of an unchanged active core.
Local taxonomic deepening occurs within the same numbered stops active in both surveys and is mostly carried by multiplicity beyond the second species.

The positive rainfall-contrast coefficients for active spatial footprint, local alpha richness and route gamma richness persist after adjustment for recorded hearing impairment, major-noise timeouts and wind, and in sensitivities adding traffic counts or using the Massachusetts noise index.

Post-opening species-trait analyses do not provide an authorized rainfall-specific mechanism: activation geometry is repeatable but fails a frozen placebo gate because reverse-direction, low-contrast and baseline-solitude rankings strongly reproduce it.
interpretation: Recent-rain conditions are associated with two-dimensional expansion of the behaviourally realized frog active community: more sampling sites become acoustically active and more species participate within both newly active and already-active sites. Local alpha and route gamma rise while measured beta-diversity metrics show no detectable shift and active-matrix fill remains practically equivalent within a frozen margin. Species-level mechanism remains unresolved; a repeatable activation-geometry candidate was demoted after reverse-direction, low-contrast and baseline-solitude placebo tests reproduced the same species ordering.

functional_response_boundary.supported: The tested conventional life-history trait space does not supply a robust mechanism for the rainfall-associated community expansion.
functional_response_boundary.not_supported: Activation geometry is not authorized as a rainfall-specific response trait because it failed the frozen placebo gate. Null or weak conventional-trait results do not establish that all unmeasured ecological or physiological traits are irrelevant.
functional_response_boundary.no_buffering_claim: Held-out response-sign diversity does not demonstrably buffer route-level richness responses.

timescale_boundary.supported: Run-level richness differs from the >=8-day rain-recency reference across 0-7 day bins, and matched support is clear through 2-3 days.
timescale_boundary.not_headline: Do not title or conclude that a week-long pulse has been identified because the >=8-day reference is sparse and the exact-consecutive matched 4-7-day contrast is imprecise.

provenance_boundary.community_extensions: post-opening analyses, each separately versioned/frozen before its own endpoint readback
provenance_boundary.no_preregistration_claim: Do not describe the alpha-beta-gamma, matrix, functional or response-diversity analyses as original preregistered hypotheses.
